author: @FrankCurzio
text:
BREAKING: Putin says the first Russian diesel tanker headed for the US sails in 2 or 3 days.

He told Trump envoy Steve Witkoff that world diesel prices fell 5-6% after the deal. Witkoff thanked him for lifting Russia's export ban.

Before Ukraine's drones hit Russia's refineries this summer, it exported about 1 million barrels of diesel a day. In early October it was 146,000, the lowest in Bloomberg's data going back to 2016.

The market isn't buying the 5-6% either.

US diesel futures jumped 5% on October 13. Retail diesel was $6.18 a gallon on October 12, up from $3.48 at the start of the year.

I think Russia banned exports because its OWN people ran short of fuel. Putin is collecting Washington's thanks for restarting sales he'd have restarted anyway.

That diesel cost is already built into everything shipped by truck - it’ll take a while to bounce back.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Wall Street & everyday traders are betting opposite ways on AI right now.

The pros keep buying crash insurance on AI companies' debt, and trading in that insurance is surging (as I flagged this morning).

Retail went all in.

A record $7 billion poured last week into one fund that triples the daily moves of chip stocks. That was 74% of all the money going into leveraged funds.

China is still buying too. ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent ordered more than 3 million Nvidia chips built to pass US export rules, worth over $35 billion at list price.

OpenAI is rushing to raise about $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation before Anthropic goes public.

My take: Anthropic is growing MUCH faster.

Its IPO could hit $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion. Putting money into OpenAI at $1.4 trillion is insane.

author: @KimizqSmile
text:
$TSLA vs. $META vs. $NVDA — The Next Big Move in AI Stocks Could Depend on Earnings
⚠️ Great earnings don't always mean higher stock prices. Expectations are everything.

Investors are increasingly asking whether the AI boom can deliver the profits needed to justify today's valuations.

Here are three stocks worth watching:

🚗 $TSLA — Tesla

The key isn't just vehicle deliveries. Investors want to see stronger margins, progress in autonomous driving, and evidence that AI and robotics can become meaningful businesses.

📱 $META — Meta Platforms

AI could improve advertising performance, user engagement, and revenue growth. But rising infrastructure spending creates another question: Will the returns justify the investment?

🧠 $NVDA — NVIDIA

NVIDIA remains central to the AI infrastructure trade. The critical factors are sustained demand, earnings growth, and whether future expectations have already been priced into the stock.

📉 The biggest lesson from earnings season:

A company can beat earnings estimates and still see its stock fall if its outlook disappoints.

That is why investors should focus on three things:

Revenue growth and profit margins.

Management's forward guidance.

Valuation versus realistic future growth.

My view: The next phase of the AI trade will be about execution, not just excitement.

The biggest winners may be companies that consistently turn AI investments into higher profits and stronger cash flow.
